source.author: lucan
source.text: Parthus per Medica rura, Sarmaticos inter campos, effusaque plano Tigridis arva solo, nulli superabilis hosti est Libertate fugae: sed non, ubi terra tumebit, Aspera conscendet montis iuga; nec per opacas Bella geret tenebras incerto debilis arcu, Nec franget nando violenti vorticis amnem, Nec tota in pugna perfusus sanguine membra Exiget aestivum calido sub pulvere solem.
source.text_original: Parthus per Medica rura, / Sarmaticos inter campos, effusaque plano / Tigridis arva solo, nulli superabilis hosti est / Libertate fugae: sed non, ubi terra tumebit, / Aspera conscendet montis iuga; nec per opacas / Bella geret tenebras incerto debilis arcu, / Nec franget nando violenti vorticis amnem, / Nec tota in pugna perfusus sanguine membra / Exiget aestivum calido sub pulvere solem.
source.text_english: The Parthian, through the Median lands, amid the Sarmatian plains and the fields of the Tigris spread out on the level ground, is invincible to no enemy by the freedom of his flight: but when the ground swells upward, he will not climb the steep ridges of a mountain; nor, feeble with his uncertain bow, will he wage war through the dark shadows; nor will he break by swimming the river of the rushing whirlpool; nor, with his limbs all drenched in blood in the whole fight, will he endure the summer sun beneath the hot dust.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hic et Naubolides tortas consurgit in undas Iphitus, hic patrium frangit Neptunius aequor qui tenet undisonam Psamathen semperque patentem Taenaron Euphemus, mollique a litore Pellae Deucalion certus iaculis et comminus ense nobilis Amphion, pariter quos edidit Hypso nec potuit similes voluitve ediscere vultus.
reuse.text_original: hic et Naubolides tortas consurgit in undas / Iphitus, hic patrium frangit Neptunius aequor / qui tenet undisonam Psamathen semperque patentem / Taenaron Euphemus, mollique a litore Pellae / Deucalion certus iaculis et comminus ense / nobilis Amphion, pariter quos edidit Hypso / nec potuit similes voluitve ediscere vultus.
reuse.text_english: Here too rises Iphitus, son of Naubolus, into the twisting waves; here Euphemus, the son of Neptune, who holds Psamathe sounding with waves and ever-open Taenarum, breaks his native sea; Deucalion from the soft shore of Pella, renowned for spears and also for the sword at close quarters; Amphion, distinguished alike by both weapons, whom Hypso bore and whose like she could not, or would not, learn to shape in face.
